# IKEA Sustainability Strategy



**The purpose of the IKEA Sustainability**
**Strategy is to inspire, activate and lead**
**us in our planning, decision-making and**
**goal‐setting so that together we can**
**achieve the changes we want to see for**
**the IKEA business and in the world.**

The IKEA Sustainability Strategy, introduced
in 2018, sets a common direction for the IKEA
franchise system and value chain and is reviewed
annually. During FY24, the strategy was updated in
accordance with our strengthened ambitions and
actions plans, and to align with the latest insights
and science.


The overall structure of our sustainability strategy,
organised into three focus areas, remains intact.
The updated ambitions for each focus area are
shown in the diagram on the right.


One important update is the shift to ‘Net Zero
and Beyond’ instead of ‘Climate positive’ as this
better reflects the next chapter of the IKEA climate
journey with strengthened climate goals, in line
with the 1.5°C target and the Net-Zero Standard by
Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi).

To better reflect the critical role of nature, the focus
area "Circular & climate" has been updated to
"Climate, nature, & circularity". The IKEA business
depends on nature for our materials, and nature
has always been an integral part of the IKEA
approach to sustainability.


**6** - IKEA SUSTAINABILITY REPORT FY24

**6** - IKEA SUSTAINABILITY REPORT FY24



Further important updates in the strategy involve
adjusting our circularity commitment as an
ongoing "transition toward a circular business",
rather than setting a fixed endpoint by 2030. This
is the same for "Aiming to use only renewable
or recycled materials by 2030", which has been
updated to "Aiming to use only renewable or
recycled materials". These revisions reflect the
evolving understanding of circular practices while
acknowledging challenges in fully achieving our
goals by 2030.

We have also adjusted our "Healthy & sustainable
living" ambition, continuing to inspire and enable
as many people as possible to move towards
healthy and sustainable lifestyles in any area
where IKEA has an influence. Since the strategy
launched in 2018, we have been unable to measure
progress towards our goal of inspiring and
enabling one billion people to live better within
the planet's boundaries. This is because the impact
on planetary boundaries is measured globally, not
individually. Our updated ambition brings us in
line with science and supports a wider approach,
committing to offer products that directly improve
a healthy and sustainable lifestyle, for example, in
the areas of energy, water, air, waste and food.

results not only validate the effectiveness of

**Reporting road safety**

IKEA supply chain operations is one of the
biggest transport buyers in the world with
around 1.7 million shipments per year. The
total distance travelled by drivers transporting
IKEA goods exceeds 400 million kilometres
yearly. We’re part of the everyday working lives
of tens of thousands of drivers who handle our
goods. As such, we have a responsibility and
an opportunity to influence the road safety
agenda in the transport industry.

Road safety is embedded in our agreements
with service providers and is a verified part
of our IWAY requirements. We continuously
engage with our service providers to increase
transparency and require reporting on
serious injuries and fatal accidents of drivers,
pedestrians or other road traffic participants
while transporting IKEA goods. This also
includes sub-contracted transport.

Based on self-reported data (not
independently verified by third parties)
shared by our road transport service
providers (excluding last-mile deliveries),
there have been five fatalities and 22 injuries
while transporting IKEA goods this year.
This gives us an initial working estimate
of our road safety performance and helps
us navigate towards the UN Sustainable
Development Goal of halving the number of
road traffic deaths and injuries.

FY24 is the first year in which we report
our road safety footprint. We are the first
cargo owner to report this type of data in
accordance with the FIA Road Safety Index.
We want to encourage a positive change
in the transport industry and promote
transparency on road safety. As a next step,
we plan to have an external assessment
of our road safety performance by FIA
to benchmark and further improve our
processes in FY25.
